## Historical audit — S0226

**Scope:** Only chunk 2 of 2 is visible. Citations below refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_1/results/r1/scene_rsi_v2_1/C2/selection/commons_194983350/trajectory.jsonl`.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Line 13, `model_request`, characters [0,195344) | The task was to reconstruct a single indoor photograph as editable SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching viewpoint and framing. The student’s inventory **interpreted** it as a café with a ceiling grid, plant shelves, banquette, table, chairs and cabinet. The image itself is not visible in this audit, so these labels and bounds are not independent observations. |
| Line 13, same range, first program and step 1 result | The program constructed multiple named assets and child primitives, including furniture, plants, architectural parts and tabletop props. It assigned colors, roughness, sheen and procedural bump, and configured camera and lights. Hierarchical inclusion shows intended part membership, not verified physical contact or geometric correctness. Step 1 reported `ok: true` and a saved render. |
| Line 13, same range, revised program and step 2 result | The student’s own comparison diagnosed oversized foreground framing and clipping. It changed lens 48 to 40, reduced table radius, compressed the sofa back, shifted and rebuilt the green chair as an arc of panels, reduced leaf size and light powers, and added ceiling color variation. These are executed changes, not independently verified improvements. Step 2 reported `ok: true`, a finished render and saved scene. |
| Line 14, `codex_session`, [0,3834); line 15, `model_response`, [0,347) | The final student session was supplied reference and two render image paths; it completed with zero tool calls and replied `DONE`. No image pixels are available here. |

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher message, diagnosis, proposed update, or evidence of teacher receipt or adoption appears in this visible chunk. The student’s render-based diagnosis and revision are autonomous work in the recorded exchange; earlier activity in the unseen chunk is unknown. The final session was read-only with shell, browser, image-viewing tools and multi-agent functionality disabled, although images were attached to the model session (line 14).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Both executions formally succeeded as builds/renders, and the student finished with `DONE`; visual or geometric correctness remains **unknown**, not established by the status or asset names. In particular, object coverage, surface appearance, chair pose, actual connections, camera alignment, lighting and remaining render defects cannot be checked without the images. The student’s clipping and washout diagnoses are hypotheses based on its comparison, not independent verification. No technical interruption, algorithm failure or empty patch is shown.

**Lessons.** Transferable: distinguish a successful render from a faithful reconstruction, and separate global framing adjustments from local geometry changes. Task-specific: the particular lens, chair shell, sofa compression and lighting changes address this student’s café interpretation; whether they improved the match remains unresolved.
